en: 2 Extraction
zh: 2　攫取

en: The root of the English word ‘plantation’ can be traced back to fourteenth-century feudal Europe, when the term was used to refer to vanguard colonial settlements, including towns, farms, and seigniories, and particularly to the establishment of settler communities and industries in overseas colonies (Moore 2010; Manjapra 2018). Natural resource extraction, alongside human displacement, imperial expansion, and territorial occupation, were thus key operatives within plantation semantics and systems from the outset. In many instances, these dynamics sit within and further dominant visions of extraction as a ‘civilizational’ process that transforms putatively ‘wild’ landscapes, together with their human and non-human dwellers, into disciplined or tamed subjects whose bodies and affordances are put to work to serve colonial and postcolonial agendas. Historically, the conjuring of extraction as a form of progress and improvement alongside a source of profit and productivity, manifested in the transformation of jungle-laden frontiers into monocrop tea plantations in imperial India and of swamp ecologies into sugarcane plantations in the colonial Caribbean. Today, this logic continues to legitimize the large-scale substitution of tropical forests for timber monocrops in Indonesia, of biodiverse marshlands for oil palm plantations in Colombia, and of subtropical grasslands for soy agro-industries in Argentina. In examining how extraction – a process often associated primarily with subterranean industrial activities such as mining – shapes plantation lifeworlds and afterlives, I invite a return to the term’s original and more expansive sense of a literal or figurative, and often coercive,
, or

in space and time that reshapes the existences and entanglements of humans and other-than-humans. Doing so uncovers extraction’s complex relationship with value and worth, as these are at times fiercely coveted and guarded, and at others discarded and invisibilized.
zh: 英语“plantation”一词的词源，可追溯至14世纪的欧洲封建社会。当时，这个词指殖民扩张前沿的定居点，包括城镇、农场与领主领地，尤其指在海外殖民地建立移民社群和产业（Moore 2010；Manjapra 2018）。因此，自然资源的攫取，以及人口迁离、帝国扩张和领土占据，从一开始就是种植园语义与制度中的关键运作因素。在许多情况下，这些动态既置身于、又推进了一种占主导地位的想象：将攫取视为“文明化”过程，把所谓“野蛮”的景观及其中的人类与非人居住者，转化为受到规训或驯服的主体，动员其身体和可供利用的能力，为殖民与后殖民议程服务。在历史上，人们既把攫取设想为利润与生产率的来源，也把它构想为进步与改良的形式；这种观念体现为帝国统治下的印度将丛林密布的边疆改造成单一茶叶种植园，以及殖民时代的加勒比地区将沼泽生态改造成甘蔗种植园。今天，同样的逻辑继续为印度尼西亚以大规模单一用材林取代热带森林、哥伦比亚以油棕种植园取代生物多样性丰富的湿地，以及阿根廷以大豆农工业取代亚热带草原提供正当性。在考察攫取——一种通常首先让人联想到采矿等地下工业活动的过程——如何塑造种植园生活世界及其后续存续时，我希望回到这个词原初而更为宽广的含义：在时空之中，发生字面意义或比喻意义上的、往往带有强制性的抽取、撤离或移除，从而重塑人类与非人存在的生存及其相互纠缠的关系。这样做，能够揭示攫取同价值及重要性之间的复杂关系：这些东西有时被极力觊觎和守护，有时又遭到丢弃与隐形化。
body.review: 底本在列举印度尼西亚、哥伦比亚与阿根廷时采用“substitution of … for …”句式，其通常语法方向与本段前后论述相反。此处依上下文译为种植园取代原有生态；英文保留底本句法。

en: 2.1 Indigenous Dispossession and Rural Displacement
zh: 2.1　原住民的土地剥夺与乡村人口迁离

en: The establishment of monocrops in (settler)-colonized world-regions was from the very outset enabled through the forceful extraction of Indigenous Peoples from lands with which they entertained intimate cultural, spiritual, and ancestral relations since time immemorial. In the early nineteenth-century American South, for example, the spread of cotton plantations, alongside tobacco and hemp industries, was facilitated by the expulsion of Native Peoples, including the Cherokee, Chickasaw, Creek, and Seminole from their homelands in Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, and North Carolina, to new territories (or reservations) west of the Mississippi River, in a process that was legally instituted and sanctioned through the Indian Removal Act of 1830. Over one-quarter of the Cherokee population alone died of cold, hunger, and disease during the relocation journey of 1838–1839, which was later designated and commemorated as the ‘Trail of Tears’ through a 1987 Act of Congress (Perdue 2012; Kennedy 2013). The imposed extraction of Indigenous Peoples from their native lands was also seminal to the establishment of sugarcane plantations in seventeenth-century Dutch-colonized Guyana, where imperial agribusiness ventures forced communities who had inhabited the Caribbean islands for some 6,000 years to retreat from the Atlantic coast to the hinterland or interior – a zone that continues to be imagined and experienced as a ‘space of underdevelopment’ (Jackson 2012) compared to areas earlier integrated into the imperial political economy. In the teeth of colonial extraction, the cultural, economic, and political power of Indigenous Peoples across the broader Caribbean region was rendered secondary to those of settler-Creoles, creating new and often-fraught identity struggles between Black and Native communities that perdure to this day.
zh: 在世界各处遭到殖民——包括移民殖民——的地区，单一种植从一开始就是通过强行将原住民族从其土地上抽离而建立起来的；自远古以来，他们便同这些土地保持着亲密的文化、精神及祖先关系。例如，在19世纪初的美国南部，棉花种植园以及烟草和大麻产业的扩张，得益于把切罗基人、奇克索人、克里克人和塞米诺尔人等原住民族，从佐治亚、亚拉巴马、田纳西和北卡罗来纳的家园驱赶到密西西比河以西的新领地或保留地。1830年的《印第安人迁移法》以法律形式确立并批准了这一过程。仅切罗基人，就有超过四分之一的人口在1838—1839年的迁移旅途中因寒冷、饥饿和疾病而死亡；1987年，美国国会通过法案，将这一历程命名为“血泪之路”，予以纪念（Perdue 2012；Kennedy 2013）。在17世纪荷兰殖民统治下的圭亚那，强行把原住民族从故土抽离，同样是建立甘蔗种植园的基础。帝国农业企业迫使那些已在加勒比诸岛居住约六千年的社群，从大西洋沿岸退往腹地或内陆；与较早融入帝国政治经济的地区相比，这片地带至今仍被想象和体验为“欠发展的空间”（Jackson 2012）。在殖民攫取的逼迫下，整个加勒比地区原住民族的文化、经济与政治权力，都被置于移民克里奥尔人之下，由此在黑人社群与原住民社群之间形成新的、往往充满张力的身份斗争，并延续至今。

en: Further south in Latin America, sugar plantations developed under sixteenth and seventeenth-century Portuguese rule were largely enabled through the systematic uprooting of various Indigenous communities, notably speakers of Tupi–Guarani languages in Northeast Brazil, some of whom were initially incorporated as labourers within sugarcane concessions but were then replaced with imported and enslaved Africans. By 1590, malnourishment, exhaustion, and diseases including measles and haemorrhagic fever, had reduced Indigenous populations to a tenth of their original numbers. The ‘structures of violence and death’ (Eichen 2020: 36) undergirding plantation proliferation thus encompassed both the conversion of Indigenous Peoples’ biodiverse native forests into imperial sources of wealth
the extraction of Indigenous Peoples themselves from the native soils, landscapes, and ecosystems that once sustained and nourished them.
zh: 再向南看，在拉丁美洲，16至17世纪葡萄牙统治下发展起来的甘蔗种植园，很大程度上以系统性地将各原住民社群连根拔起为条件，尤其涉及巴西东北部说图皮—瓜拉尼诸语言的社群。其中一些人起初被纳入甘蔗特许经营区充当劳工，随后却被输入的、遭到奴役的非洲人取代。到1590年，营养不良、筋疲力尽，以及麻疹、出血热等疾病，已使原住民人口减少至原来的十分之一。因此，支撑种植园扩张的“暴力与死亡结构”（Eichen 2020: 36），既包含把原住民族生物多样性丰富的本土森林转化为帝国财富来源，也包含把原住民族自身从曾经维系和滋养他们的故土、景观与生态系统中抽离。

en: Importantly, plantation expansion across these and other colonial periods and geographies did not operate in a silo but rather sat within a larger nexus of imperial projects seeking to assert physical and political control over colonies as natural resources and over colonized subjects as targets of displacement, eradication, and/or exploitation – from mining, urbanization, militarization, and road and other infrastructural developments to enforced missionization, formal education, and cultural assimilation. Today, many plantations in the Global South remain predicated on extraction and occupation as the axiomatic premises for the enhancement of productivity and profit, albeit often framed in the language of globalization, modernization, national economic growth, and regional and rural poverty alleviation.
zh: 需要强调的是，在这些以及其他殖民时期和地区，种植园扩张并非孤立运作，而是置身于更庞大的帝国工程网络之中。这些工程试图在物质与政治层面确立控制：把殖民地当作自然资源，把被殖民者当作迁移、消灭和／或剥削的对象。它们包括采矿、城市化、军事化、道路及其他基础设施建设，也包括强制传教、正规教育与文化同化。今天，全球南方许多种植园仍把攫取与占据当作提高生产率和利润的不证自明的前提，只不过常常以全球化、现代化、国家经济增长，以及区域和乡村减贫的语言来表述。

en: In present-day Cambodia, for instance, up to 800,000 people have suffered from land conflicts, livelihood losses, and forced displacement following the establishment of Economic Land Concessions (ELCs), a long-term lease mechanism that allows beneficiaries to clear land in order to develop industrial agriculture and that was revived by the Cambodian government in the 1990s to enhance foreign investment and economic development. Related government policies that encourage populations displaced by ELCs to resettle in peripheral territories that are classified as ‘unused’ or ‘unoccupied’ under state legislation have prompted intensifying conflict between incoming migrants and local communities (Han & McAndrew 2018). ELCs have had particularly marked impacts among rural ethnic minorities in Cambodia, many of whom depend on the natural environment for their income and subsistence, including through rice paddy cultivation, small-scale agriculture, and swidden farming. Industrial rubber, cassava, sugarcane, banana, and other plantation trees have been planted by national and foreign leaseholders in lieu of these traditional, smallholder farming systems, often without consulting or seeking the consent of local landholders, and with dire repercussions on their collective food security and food sovereignty.
zh: 例如，在当代柬埔寨，随着“经济土地特许经营权”（Economic Land Concessions，简称ELCs）的设立，多达八十万人遭受土地冲突、生计丧失与强迫迁移。ELCs是一种长期租赁机制，允许获益者清理土地、发展工业化农业；柬埔寨政府在20世纪90年代恢复这一机制，以促进外国投资与经济发展。相关政府政策鼓励因ELCs而迁离的人口，重新安置到国家法律划为“未使用”或“无人占用”的边缘地区，结果促使新迁入者与当地社群之间的冲突不断加剧（Han & McAndrew 2018）。ELCs对柬埔寨乡村少数族群的影响尤其显著。他们许多人依靠自然环境获得收入、维持生计，包括种植水稻、经营小规模农业和从事刀耕火种式轮耕。本国与外国承租者种下工业化橡胶、木薯、甘蔗、香蕉及其他种植园作物，取代这些传统小农耕作体系；这一过程往往没有同当地土地持有者协商，也未征求其同意，并严重损害了他们集体的粮食安全与食物主权。

en: A similar process of enforced rural relocation has been documented in the arid and drought-prone regions of Northeast Ethiopia, where the establishment of cotton and sugarcane plantations has been accompanied by the development of hydroelectric dams for irrigation purposes, with devastating impacts on the water and land access of Afar and Oromo pastoralists who use the floodplains of the Awash Valley for dry-season grazing. These communities have been displaced to a total of 20,000 and now face severe food insecurity – at times, famine – due to their dislocation from their prior subsistence and grazing grounds (Stevenson & Buffavand 2018). In this and many comparable instances, the forced removal (direct or indirect) of Indigenous Peoples and other rural communities from their homelands has been facilitated by laws that were instituted under colonial rule and whose legacies find expression in current policies that continue to classify Indigenous lands as ‘terra nullius’ and that either do not recognize Indigenous Peoples’ existence or do so on the basis of externally imposed criteria rather than on the principle of self-determination enshrined in international human rights law.
zh: 在埃塞俄比亚东北部干旱且易遭旱灾的地区，也有类似强制乡村迁移过程的记录。棉花与甘蔗种植园的建立，伴随着服务灌溉用途的水电大坝建设，对阿法尔与奥罗莫牧民获取水源和土地造成毁灭性影响；这些牧民原本利用阿瓦什河谷的洪泛平原进行旱季放牧。这些社群已有总计两万人被迫迁离；由于离开原先维持生计和放牧的土地，他们如今面临严重的粮食不安全，有时甚至遭遇饥荒（Stevenson & Buffavand 2018）。在这一案例及许多相似情形中，殖民统治下建立的法律，便利了以直接或间接方式强迫原住民族及其他乡村社群离开家园。这些法律的遗产体现在当今政策之中：政策继续将原住民土地划为“无主地”（terra nullius），或者不承认原住民族的存在，或者依照外部强加的标准予以承认，而非依据国际人权法所确立的自决原则。

en: One striking example of this is Indonesia, the world’s top palm oil-producing country. Seventy-five years after Indonesian independence, agrarian laws introduced by the Dutch in the mid-eighteenth century, and particularly the legal concept of ‘free state domain’ (domein verklaring) instituted to promote private investment, continue to leave ambiguous the question of where state claims over land end and community claims begin. This legal opacity radically undermines the tenurial security of rural populations inhabiting or forcibly removed from lands converted to timber, oil palm, and other commodity plantation zones. While Indonesian laws do recognize ‘custom’ (adat) as a source of juridical authority and ‘customary law communities’ (masyarakat hukum adat) as a local expression of Indigeneity, these legal instruments remain premised on a system of land rights inherited from the Napoleonic civil codes of continental Europe – one that ultimately weakens pre-existing communal tenures and strengthens the state’s prerogative of control by privileging national economic interests over customary and Indigenous rights (Colchester, Chao and Anderson 2024).
zh: 世界最大的棕榈油生产国印度尼西亚，是一个鲜明的例子。印度尼西亚独立七十五年后，荷兰人在18世纪中叶引入的土地法，尤其是为促进私人投资而确立的“无权利负担的国有土地”（domein verklaring）法律概念，仍使国家土地权利主张止于何处、社群权利主张始于何处的问题含混不清。这种法律上的不透明，严重损害了乡村人口的土地持有安全：他们居住的土地，或他们被迫离开的土地，已被改造成用材林、油棕及其他商品作物种植园地带。虽然印度尼西亚法律承认“习惯”（adat）是司法权威的来源，也把“习惯法社群”（masyarakat hukum adat）视为原住民性的地方表达，但这些法律工具仍以继承自欧洲大陆拿破仑民法典的土地权利制度为前提。该制度把国家经济利益置于习惯权利与原住民权利之上，最终削弱既有的共同体土地持有制度，并强化国家的控制特权（Colchester, Chao and Anderson 2024）。
body.review: 底本确为“18世纪中叶”及引注2024。书末参考文献第67页相应条目却为2014年《Assault on the Commons》；已核对该报告版权页，确为2014年，报告第15页把殖民国家土地归属宣告定于1870年。Jeffrey Neilson在2020年专文中亦将domein verklaring追溯至1870年。这里保留底本年代与引注，并提示其不一致。

en: In other contexts, plantation proliferation through Indigenous displacement and rural dispossession is buttressed by prior histories of civil war and guerrilla violence as well as by ongoing realities of para-military occupation. This is the case in Colombia, where intensive deforestation and oil palm expansion are taking place against the backdrop of a perduring armed conflict that has displaced over five million people since 1964. In the region of Bajo Atrato, large-scale plantation developments, purportedly motivated by the expulsion of illegal guerrilla groups, have resulted in the displacement of an estimated 15,000 Afro-Colombian inhabitants, while concomitantly offering a legal basis and justification for counterinsurgency groups to launder capital, strengthen their economic base, and secure their territorial presence in the region (Torres Mora 2020). Across these and many other plantation geographies and histories, the violent removal of Indigenous peoples and rural communities from their native homelands and soils forms a fundamental premise for agro-industrial expansion. Extirpations of people from place to make way for monocrops are intimately tied to the extractivist logic of plantations’ own
mechanisms of commodity production, which I turn to next.
zh: 在其他情境中，通过原住民迁离和乡村土地剥夺实现的种植园扩张，还得到既往内战与游击战争暴力历史，以及持续存在的准军事占领现实的支撑。哥伦比亚便是如此：大规模毁林与油棕扩张，发生在一场持久武装冲突的背景下；自1964年以来，这场冲突已使五百多万人流离失所。在巴霍阿特拉托地区，大规模种植园开发声称以驱逐非法游击组织为目的，却造成估计一万五千名非裔哥伦比亚居民迁离；同时，它又为反叛乱武装洗钱、增强经济基础并巩固在当地的领土存在，提供法律依据与正当理由（Torres Mora 2020）。在这些以及其他众多种植园地理和历史情境中，以暴力把原住民族与乡村社群从其故乡和土地上移除，是农工业扩张的根本前提。为了给单一种植让路而把人从地方连根拔起，与种植园自身内部商品生产机制的攫取主义逻辑密切相连。下文就转向这一问题。

en: 2.2 Enslavement and Exploitation
zh: 2.2　奴役与剥削

en: Central to the internal operations of the plantation system is the extraction of labour from workers who were either translocated into foreign agro-industrial topographies under colonial enslavement regimes, forced to migrate and seek plantation employment as a means of economic survival in the absence or loss of alternative livelihoods, or incorporated into agribusiness labour systems established on their own native soils. No period in human history illustrates the first of these processes more vividly than the trans-Atlantic slave trade, which has been recognized by the United Nations as ‘the greatest crime against humanity committed in what is now defined as the modern era’ (Missouri Sherman-Peter 2022).
zh: 种植园体系内部运作的核心，是从劳动者身上攫取劳动。这些劳动者可能在殖民奴役体制下被转移到异国的农工业地带；可能由于没有其他生计，或失去了其他生计，被迫迁移、寻求种植园就业以维持经济生存；也可能被纳入在自己故土上建立起来的农业企业劳动体系。人类历史中，没有哪个时期比跨大西洋奴隶贸易更鲜明地展现上述第一种过程。联合国已将这一贸易认定为“如今所谓现代时期所犯下的最严重反人类罪行”（Missouri Sherman-Peter 2022）。
body.review: 本书所引2022年材料，是加勒比共同体常驻联合国观察员A. Missouri Sherman-Peter发表于《联合国纪事》的署名文章。此处保留作者“联合国认定”的表述，但不把署名评论与联合国决议或司法裁判等同；原文引句及下段人口区间均见该文的可检索开篇。

en: Spanning over 300 years, the trans-Atlantic slave trade of 1501–1867 saw some 12 to 20 million African men, women, and children kidnapped, uprooted from their homes, transported on European and American ships as human cargo, and trafficked across the Atlantic Ocean to work under conditions of enslavement in imperial cotton, rubber, jute, tobacco, and sugarcane plantations. Known as the ‘Middle Passage’, this journey fed and fuelled plantations established by English, French, Dutch, Spanish, and Danish colonists, with chattel slavery instituted through the Slave Code of 1661. Originally developed in Barbados by the English colonial assembly and later adopted as the template across North American colonies (Rugemer 2013), this Code laid the juridical and moral basis for the enslavement of Africans by defining them as non-human bare flesh and fungible property, readily available for ownership and trade by White purchasers (Spillers 1987; Wynter 2003; King 2016).
zh: 从1501年至1867年，持续三百多年的跨大西洋奴隶贸易，使约一千二百万至两千万非洲男性、女性和儿童遭绑架，被从家中连根拔起，作为人类货物装上欧洲和美洲船只，贩运过大西洋，在帝国的棉花、橡胶、黄麻、烟草与甘蔗种植园中受到奴役、从事劳动。这段被称为“中间航程”的旅途，为英国、法国、荷兰、西班牙和丹麦殖民者建立的种植园不断输送动力与生命；1661年的《奴隶法典》则将动产奴隶制制度化。该法典最初由巴巴多斯的英国殖民议会制定，后来成为北美各殖民地采用的范本（Rugemer 2013）。它把非洲人界定为非人的赤裸肉身和可相互替换的财产，供白人买家随时占有和交易，从而为奴役非洲人奠定法律与道德基础（Spillers 1987；Wynter 2003；King 2016）。

en: Over 20 per cent of Africans who crossed the Atlantic Ocean aboard colonial ships died of hunger, disease, exhaustion, and abuse before reaching the shores of the United States and the Caribbean. Awaiting those who survived the journey was an egregiously violent regime of labour extraction that was premised on the exploitability of racialized, dehumanized, and commodified Black bodies. This regime was imposed not only on those individuals brought over from the African continent but also on their offspring, with Black women’s reproduction subject to enforced breeding regimes that sought to secure plantations’ future labour supply (Morgan 2004). Resistance to the abusive conditions of plantation labour in colonial monocrops was routinely met with horrific physical and psychological violence, including public displays of torture, humiliation, and murder (Hartman 1997). In nineteenth-century banana and sugarcane plantations in Central America and Hawai‘i, respectively, such resistance was countered through the intentional social division of work across different ethnic groups, which served a divide-and-control function anchored in the conjuring of racialized prejudices, hierarchies, and rivalries between Amerindian, West Indian immigrants, and Central American Hispanics on the one hand (Bourgois 1989) and between East Asians, Norwegians, Puerto Ricans, and Portuguese on the other (Takaki 1983).
zh: 在乘殖民船只横渡大西洋的非洲人中，超过20%尚未抵达美国和加勒比地区的海岸，就因饥饿、疾病、疲惫与虐待而死亡。等待那些熬过航程者的，是一套极端暴力的劳动攫取体制；它以经过种族化、非人化和商品化的黑人身体之可剥削性为前提。这一体制不仅施加于从非洲大陆运来的人，也施加于他们的后代。黑人女性的生育被纳入强迫繁殖体制，以确保种植园未来的劳动力供应（Morgan 2004）。在殖民地单一种植体系中，对种植园虐待性劳动条件的抵抗，常常遭到骇人的身体与心理暴力镇压，包括公开施行酷刑、羞辱与谋杀（Hartman 1997）。19世纪，中美洲的香蕉种植园与夏威夷的甘蔗种植园，分别通过有意在不同族群间划分社会劳动，来压制这种抵抗。这种分化与控制机制，依靠的是制造种族化的偏见、等级与敌对：在中美洲，它发生于美洲原住民、西印度群岛移民与中美洲西班牙裔之间（Bourgois 1989）；在夏威夷，则发生于东亚人、挪威人、波多黎各人与葡萄牙人之间（Takaki 1983）。

en: In a devious instrumentalization of perceived human-vegetal affinities, labour extraction on colonial plantations often operated on the assumption that enslaved or exploited people were best suited to the conditions of plantation work and the proclivities of the particular plants cultivated. In eighteenth-century Kentucky, for example, hemp was often described as a ‘nigger crop’, its biotic recalcitrance, marshy growth environments, and colossal labour requirements said to be ideal work for ‘negros’, who were in any case as ‘dirty’ as the process required to manage and process the plant itself (Hopkins 1951: 24). These beliefs continue to undergird contemporary plantation labour regimes, wherein racial traits and social-evolutionary ideologies are deployed to justify or naturalize the exploitation of some populations over others. In the Paraguayan soy sector, for instance the unwieldy plant of cotton is frequently described as a crop best cultivated by brown peasants or ‘campesinos’, and the modern plant of soy by White people (Hetherington 2019). In the Ecuadorian flower sector, meanwhile, participation in plantation labour is often framed by agribusiness operators as a means of uplifting and civilizing Indigenous peoples from their primitive ways of life, in a form of racial emancipation and liberation (Krupa 2022). This dynamic echoes in uncanny ways the discourses of agronomists and government officials in Malaysia at the turn of the twentieth century, wherein the scientific care of oil palm plants and plantations was thought to presuppose care of the ‘native’, providing a necessary corrective to what were percieved as ‘careless’ local modes of cultivation and production (Rudge 2022).
zh: 殖民种植园的劳动攫取，常常狡黠地把想象中的人与植物的亲缘关系工具化，其前提是：受奴役或遭剥削的人，最适应种植园的劳动条件，以及特定栽培植物的习性。例如，在18世纪的肯塔基，大麻常被称为“黑鬼作物”；据称，它难以驯服的生物特性、沼泽般的生长环境，以及极大的劳动需求，使之成为“黑人”的理想工作。反正，按照这种观念，黑人和照料、加工这种植物的过程一样“肮脏”（Hopkins 1951: 24）。这些信念继续支撑着当代种植园的劳动体制：人们动用种族特征和社会进化论意识形态，为相对于其他群体而剥削某些人口群体辩护，或使这种剥削显得理所当然。例如，在巴拉圭的大豆产业中，难以料理的棉花常被说成最适合棕色皮肤农民——即campesinos——种植的作物，而现代化的大豆则被说成适合白人种植（Hetherington 2019）。与此同时，在厄瓜多尔的花卉产业中，农业企业经营者常把参与种植园劳动描绘为提升原住民、使其摆脱原始生活方式而走向文明的途径，并称之为种族解放（Krupa 2022）。这一动态以令人不安的方式，呼应了20世纪之交马来亚农学家与政府官员的话语：他们认为，对油棕植物和种植园的科学照料，须以照料“土著”为前提，为被视作“漫不经心”的当地栽培与生产方式提供必要纠正（Rudge 2022）。
body.review: 本段含作者为批判殖民种族主义而引述的历史蔑称，并非译者或作者对群体的称呼。底本英语percieved为perceived的拼写倒置，英文整理版仍保留底本文字。底本此处作Malaysia；译文依其20世纪之交语境使用历史地域称谓“马来亚”。

en: In other contexts, the relocation of people from their native homelands to industrial plantations is less a process imposed by agribusiness operators or the state, but rather a means of economic survival sought out by precarious communities themselves and often tied to the promise of wealth and opportunity. A case in point is the Malaysian oil palm industry (formerly the world’s largest palm oil-producing country) that relies on an estimated one million migrant workers employed on estates and mills in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah. Most of these workers hail from Indonesia, notably the less-developed islands of Sumatra, Sulawesi, Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores. Many eke out a precarious existence dependent on insecure, casualized, and flexibilized work arrangements including sub-contracted labour and low/piece-rate wages. National laws prohibit migrant workers from settling permanently in Malaysia, acquiring Malaysian citizenship, influencing Malaysian culture, marrying Malaysians, or sending their children to local schools. Workers’ captivity to plantation employers’ biopolitical control is further exacerbated by the confiscation of their passports, debt bondage, the selling and reselling of migrant workers by brokers, and the risks of deportation, physical punishment, and imprisonment (Pye et al. 2012). These dynamics position agribusiness plantations as just one of many manifestations of racialized regimes of extraction globally – from clothing and technology manufacturing sweatshops to the industrial livestock and dairy industry, oil, gas, mineral, and coal mining, and many other sectors sustained through relations of exploitative labour – that might not constitute literal monocrops, but that nonetheless trace their origins back to plantation logics and that continue in fields and factories around the world (Chao, Wolford, Ofstehage et al. 2024, 13).
zh: 在另一些情境中，人们从故乡迁入工业化种植园，与其说是农业企业经营者或国家强加的过程，不如说是处境不稳的社群自己寻求经济生存的手段；它往往又同财富和机会的许诺相连。马来西亚的油棕产业就是一个例子。这个国家曾是世界最大的棕榈油生产国，其位于马来半岛、砂拉越和沙巴的庄园与加工厂，依靠估计一百万名移民工人。这些工人大多来自印度尼西亚，尤其是发展程度较低的苏门答腊、苏拉威西、龙目、松巴哇和弗洛勒斯诸岛。许多人依靠缺乏保障、临时化与灵活化的工作安排勉强谋生，包括分包劳动，以及低工资或计件工资。国家法律禁止移民工人在马来西亚永久定居、取得马来西亚公民身份、影响马来西亚文化、与马来西亚人结婚，或把子女送入当地学校。护照遭没收、债务束缚、中介对移民工人的反复转卖，以及被遣返、遭体罚和入狱的风险，又进一步加剧了工人受制于种植园雇主生命政治控制的处境（Pye et al. 2012）。这些动态表明，农业企业的种植园，只是全球种族化攫取体制的诸多表现之一。其他表现包括服装与技术产品制造业的血汗工厂、工业化畜牧和乳品业、石油、天然气、矿物及煤炭开采，以及许多依靠剥削性劳动关系维系的行业。它们或许并非字面意义上的单一种植体系，但仍可将其起源追溯到种植园逻辑，而这种逻辑继续存在于世界各地的田野和工厂之中（Chao, Wolford, Ofstehage et al. 2024, 13）。
body.review: 本段法律限制依作者及所引2012年研究译出，不据此认定所有移民身份在当下均适用同一法律规则；具体法规、许可类别与实施时期尚待逐项核验。

en: The extractive logic of plantation labour has long been paired with its attritive effects on the physical and reproductive health of agribusiness workers – a reality that comes to light vividly in the context of prevalent pesticide use within the monocrop sector. Particularly prominent among these non-human chemical actors is paraquat, a carcinogenic herbicide that has been linked to kidney and liver failure as well as Parkinson’s disease. Banned in over fifty countries, paraquat continues to be used in plantations across the Global North and South, notably in palm oil operations in Southeast Asia. Another prevalent chemical is dibromo-3-chloropropane, or DBCP, the active ingredient in the nematicide Nemagon, which has caused thousands of banana plantation workers in Costa Rica and Honduras to suffer from severe and long-term health conditions include sterility and cancer (Soluri 2005). Elsewhere, including in Martinique and Guadeloupe, it is the pesticide chlordécone (‘kepone’ in English) that poisons the bodies of banana plantation workers, alongside the islands’ soils and sources of water. Originally produced in the United States to combat the effects of the parasitic banana borer beetle, this hormone-altering substance is a major driver of male infertility and prostate cancer among workers whose exposure to the toxin is aggravated by the lack of protective equipment or sanitary measures (Agard-Jones 2013).
zh: 种植园劳动的攫取逻辑，长期伴随着对农业企业工人身体健康与生殖健康的损耗。在单一种植领域广泛使用农药的背景下，这一现实尤为清楚。在这些非人的化学行动者中，百草枯尤其突出；它是一种致癌除草剂，与肾衰竭、肝衰竭以及帕金森病有关。尽管已被五十多个国家禁用，百草枯仍继续用于全球北方与全球南方的种植园，尤其是东南亚棕榈油生产活动。另一种普遍使用的化学品是二溴氯丙烷，即DBCP；它是杀线虫剂Nemagon的有效成分，已使哥斯达黎加与洪都拉斯数千名香蕉种植园工人遭受包括不育和癌症在内的严重、长期健康损害（Soluri 2005）。在马提尼克和瓜德罗普等其他地方，毒害香蕉种植园工人身体，以及岛上土壤与水源的，则是农药十氯酮，法语称chlordécone，英语称kepone。它最初在美国生产，用于对付寄生性的香蕉蛀甲虫；这种改变激素作用的物质，是工人男性不育和前列腺癌的重要致因。由于缺乏防护装备或卫生措施，他们接触毒物的程度又被进一步加重（Agard-Jones 2013）。
body.review: “致癌”及其余健康判断均为底本表述。百草枯的急性毒性与长期疾病因果判断应予区分：Tanner等2011年病例对照研究发现其使用与帕金森病呈正相关；美国EPA当前页面则指出研究结果并不一致，尚未认定按标签使用所致暴露与帕金森病或癌症之间存在明确联系。此处保留原文，并不将关联或作者判断改写成一致的医学定论。底本conditions include亦原样保留。

en: In California’s strawberry plantations, meanwhile, pathogenic control through regular fumigation and consequent pesticide drift is a primary cause of breathing difficulties, nausea, burning, and headaches among Latino migrant workers, who are ineligible for income support until they are completely disabled and who are reticent to call out pesticides’ adverse health effects for fear of being fired or deported (Guthman 2019). In these and other instances, the promotion of ill-regulated chemical use in plantation landscapes points to a privileging of cash crops’ health and productivity over the physical and intergenerational wellbeing of plantation labourers, whose extractive potential is paired with their inherent disposability and replaceability in the generation of capital and surplus – all within a broader system that relies on and maintains global as well as local wealth and racial inequalities. But humans are not the only ones subject to such extractive regimes. So too are plants themselves, as objects of biotechnological manipulation and forms of lively capital.
zh: 与此同时，在加利福尼亚的草莓种植园，为控制病原体而反复熏蒸，以及由此产生的农药飘移，是拉丁裔移民工人呼吸困难、恶心、灼痛与头痛的主要原因。他们只有在完全失去劳动能力后，才有资格获得收入补助；又由于害怕被解雇或遣返，不愿公开指出农药的不良健康影响（Guthman 2019）。在这些以及其他情形中，种植园景观内对监管不足的化学品使用的推广，显示出一种优先次序：经济作物的健康与生产率，高于种植园劳动者的身体及跨代福祉。在资本与剩余的生成过程中，劳动者可被攫取的潜能，同他们被视为本就可以丢弃、可以替换的地位相结合；而这一切，都发生在一个依赖并维持全球及地方财富不平等与种族不平等的更大体系之中。但受到这些攫取体制支配的，并不只有人类。植物自身也同样如此：它们是生物技术操控的对象，也是活性资本的形式。

en: 2.3 The Labour of Plantation Crops and Ecologies
zh: 2.3　种植园作物与生态的劳动

en: To think about plants as objects of extraction is to draw attention to the metabolic labours that vegetal beings perform in generating the products of plantation economies – whether it be their fruit, sap, trunks, nuts, or seeds. Sustaining these non-human metabolic labours requires an understanding of plants’ processes of growth and senescence, their photosynthetic affordances, their vegetative or sexual reproduction, as well as the soil, water, nutrient, and climate requirements needed to support intensive and large-scale cultivation. While the metabolic labours of plants might be anchored in empirically grounded, scientific epistemologies including botany, agronomy, and biology, they have also been widely harnessed to further racial configurations of plantation labour and colonial-capitalist technologies of land expansion and yield intensification. Attending to more-than-human forms of work thus matters in uncovering what cash crops demand of humans in terms of management, nurture, and care. But it also sheds light on how humans have instrumentalized plants’ biotic and ecosystemic affordances to legitimize their manipulation or transformation in the name of productivity and profitability, and to buttress regimes of human exploitation, social inequality, and racial violence.
zh: 把植物视为攫取的对象，就是要关注植物存在为了生成种植园经济的产品——无论果实、树液、树干、坚果还是种子——而付出的代谢劳动。维系这些非人的代谢劳动，需要理解植物的生长与衰老过程、光合作用能力、营养繁殖或有性繁殖，以及支撑集约化、大规模栽培所需的土壤、水分、养分和气候条件。植物的代谢劳动固然可以立足于有实证基础的科学认识论，包括植物学、农学和生物学，但人们也广泛利用它们，进一步推行种植园劳动的种族化配置，以及服务于土地扩张和增产的殖民—资本主义技术。因此，关注超越人类的工作形式，有助于揭示经济作物对人的管理、培育和照料提出了什么要求。但这也说明，人类如何把植物的生物能力和生态系统可供性工具化，以生产率与盈利能力之名，为对植物的操控或改造提供正当性，并支撑剥削人类、制造社会不平等与施加种族暴力的体制。

en: Take the cotton plantations of the nineteenth-century Southern United States. The high nutrient and soil demands of large-scale cotton plantations, identified in scientific studies of the time, together with the crop’s notorious vulnerability to pests and parasites, were at first remedied through the acquisition of ever-greater swaths of land and subsequently through the importation of guano and the introduction of synthetic pesticides and fertilizers. The recognition that intensive plantation agriculture depleted soil quality later served to justify the deployment of enslaved workers not only to work in plantations but also to mine marl (a sedimentary rock containing lime) without payment or compensation. In this ‘chemicalization of slavery’, the productive value of enslaved people was equated to the fertility-boosting qualities of inanimate matter, including soils, minerals, and faeces (Williams & Porter 2022: 505).
zh: 以19世纪美国南部的棉花种植园为例。当时的科学研究发现，大规模棉花种植园对养分和土壤条件的要求很高，而棉花又因易受虫害和寄生生物侵袭而著称。人们最初通过获取越来越大片的土地来应对这些问题，后来则转向输入鸟粪，以及引入合成农药与化肥。认识到集约化种植园农业会损耗土壤质量，后来又成为一种正当化理由：受奴役的劳动者不仅被派去在种植园工作，还被迫在毫无报酬或补偿的情况下，开采泥灰岩——一种含石灰质的沉积岩。在这种“奴隶制的化学化”过程中，受奴役者的生产价值，被等同于土壤、矿物和粪便等无生命物质提高肥力的性质（Williams & Porter 2022: 505）。

en: In the colonial Caribbean, it was the perishability of sugar – notably its high susceptibility to degradation through fermentation – that legitimized alterations to processing technologies and divisions of labour. This included the association of racialized bodies with specific tasks in the sugar production chain and the pursuit of biochemical purity through the exploitation of Black people, who were paradoxically tasked with whitening sugar by purging it of dark impurities through their enforced and often dangerous labour in mills and refineries (Rood 2017). In mid twentieth-century Liberia, meanwhile, the extraction of rubber – or ‘white gold’, as it was commonly referred to – relied on Black tappers’ intimate understanding of how deep and wide to cut the trunk in order to extract the sap without damaging the tree’s regenerative abilities (see Figure 2). Failure to achieve this would lead to loss of employment and corporal punishment for the labourers tasked with the tapping (Mitman 2021).
zh: 在殖民时期的加勒比地区，糖容易变质——尤其容易通过发酵而降解——这一性质，为加工技术和劳动分工的改变提供了正当性。其中包括把种族化的身体同制糖生产链上的特定任务联系起来，以及通过剥削黑人来追求生物化学意义上的纯度。矛盾的是，这些黑人被迫在糖厂与精炼厂从事往往十分危险的劳动，负责清除糖中的深色杂质，使糖变白（Rood 2017）。与此同时，在20世纪中叶的利比里亚，橡胶——通常被称为“白色黄金”——的采集，依靠黑人割胶工人的细致知识：树干应割多深、多宽，才能采得树液而不损害树木的再生能力（见图2）。一旦做不到这一点，负责割胶的劳动者就会失去工作，并遭到体罚（Mitman 2021）。

en: Plants’ biotic affordances also come to determine human labour patterns in contemporary plantation systems. In tea monocultures in India, for instance, workers engaged in continuous leaf plucking throughout the year are necessary to meet the continuous sprouting of tea leaves in rhythms of ‘flush’, a pause which causes sprouts to mature and therefore spoils the quality of the final product (Barua 2023). In the Southeast Asian palm oil sector in contrast, ad hoc, casualized, or seasonal work arrangements that involve low unit labour requirements and create economic precarity are driven by the slow production cycle of the oil palm plant itself, whose fruit yield does not peak until the ninth year, requires harvesting every two weeks, and begins to decline around the fifteen-year mark. For oil palm smallholders, meanwhile, the imperative to process fresh fruit bunches within forty-eight hours of picking to avoid oil acidification and spoilage often positions them in monopsonistic relations with the mills that they depend upon to process their harvest, but that are owned and operated by private corporations (Cramb & McCarthy 2016).
zh: 在当代种植园体系中，植物的生物能力也会决定人类劳动的模式。例如，在印度的单一茶叶种植园，茶叶按照一轮轮“萌发”的节律不断长出新芽，因此需要工人全年不停地采摘；采摘一旦中断，新芽就会长老，从而损害最终产品的品质（Barua 2023）。相比之下，在东南亚棕榈油产业中，临时性、零工化或季节性的工作安排，单位劳动投入要求较低，也造成经济上的不稳定；推动这些安排的，是油棕本身缓慢的生产周期。它的果实产量到第九年才达到高峰，需要每两周采收一次，大约十五年后开始下降。与此同时，油棕小农必须在采摘后四十八小时内加工新鲜果串，以避免油脂酸化和变质；这种要求常常使他们与加工厂形成买方垄断关系：他们依赖加工厂处理收成，而加工厂却由私营公司拥有和运营（Cramb & McCarthy 2016）。

zh: 图2　橡胶树干上斜向割胶切口的特写。图片提供：Lucia Barreiros Silva。

en: In other cases, optimizing the extraction of profit from cash crops has prompted human-driven modifications of plantation ecologies through the introduction of so-called ‘beneficial species’, whose activities play a key role in enhancing plant health and productivity within biological pest and parasite management programmes. For example, the damaging effects of rat infestations in Indonesian oil palm plantations are now increasingly controlled through the introduction of predator species, including leopard cats, Asian palm civets, snakes, and diurnal birds such as the yellow-bellied prinia, lesser coucal, ashy tailorbird, great tit, Oriental magpie-robin, and barn owls, which are bred in rearing centres and then released into the plantations. The deadly effects of the parasitic rhinoceros beetle are kept at bay through the actions of yellow assassin bugs, tachinid flies, and chalcidoid wasps that prey on the beetle’s eggs, and the introduction of entomopathogenic microorganisms, including various fungi, bacteria, and nonoccluded RNA viruses, that attack the epidermal cells of the beetle’s larvae (Chao 2021a). Comparable enlistings of mutualistic non-human organisms are at play within coconut plantations in the Philippines, where native kiwot bees are intentionally bred to stimulate the pollination of coconut trees, with a reported 80 per cent enhanced yield (Conde 2020). These plantations are also home to cattle herds that are locally known as ‘sweepers’ or ‘brushers’ and that, under the so-called ‘cattle under coconuts’ system, provide key ecological services by grazing on weeds, grasses, and undergrowth, thus preventing nutrient and moisture competition with coconut palms and naturally fertilizing the soil with their manure (Plucknett 1979).
zh: 在另一些情形中，为了尽可能从经济作物中攫取利润，人类通过引入所谓“有益物种”，改造种植园的生态。在虫害与寄生生物的生物防治方案中，这些物种的活动对提高植物健康水平和生产率发挥着关键作用。例如，印度尼西亚油棕种植园的鼠害，如今越来越多地通过引入捕食者加以控制，包括豹猫、椰子狸、蛇，以及黄腹鹪莺、小鸦鹃、灰缝叶莺、大山雀、鹊鸲和仓鸮等昼行鸟类。这些动物在繁育中心养殖后，被释放到种植园中。为遏制寄生性犀金龟的致命危害，人们利用捕食其虫卵的黄色猎蝽、寄蝇和小蜂，并引入包括各种真菌、细菌及非包涵体RNA病毒在内的昆虫病原微生物，攻击其幼虫的表皮细胞（Chao 2021a）。在菲律宾的椰子种植园中，也有类似的做法，把互利共生的非人生物纳入生产：当地的kiwot蜂被有意繁育，用以促进椰树授粉，据报道可使产量提高80%（Conde 2020）。这些种植园还饲养牛群，当地称之为“清扫者”或“清刷者”。在所谓“椰林养牛”体系中，牛通过啃食杂草、牧草及林下植被，提供关键的生态服务，避免这些植物与椰树争夺养分和水分，并以粪便天然地为土壤增肥（Plucknett 1979）。
body.review: 底本将仓鸮列入“昼行鸟类”，并写作“非包涵体RNA病毒”；此处保留其分类与核酸名称，提示生物学表述待核。ICTV将椰犀金龟裸病毒（Oryctes rhinoceros nudivirus）列为双链DNA病毒，不能直接等同于本段所写的RNA病毒。底本未给出这些RNA病毒的具体名称，故不擅自替换。

en: An arguably more controversial means of enhancing the extractive potential of cash crops than the ecological engineering described above takes the form of genetic modification (GM), a practice that took root in the late twentieth century following the discovery of DNA structure and subsequent scientific experimentation in gene cutting and recombination. Following the ‘Green Revolution’ and the inception of large-scale agriculture in soybean, maize, cotton, canola, and other plantation commodities across the Global South, transgenic crops were developed for the purposes of achieving stronger herbicide tolerance and pest resistance, and later came to be widely promoted in agronomic and policy discourse as key to sustaining the food security of developing nation-states (Conway 2012). Their proliferation, however, has and continues to be contested on multiple grounds.These include GM crops’ potentially harmful impacts on consumer and environmental health, their detrimental effects on indigenous plant and agricultural intellectual property rights and patenting opportunities, their adverse consequences for small-scale farmers’ economic empowerment and market access, and their implications for plants themselves as lifeforms subject to ethically questionable and primarily corporate-led agri-bio-technological manipulation and homogenization.
zh: 与上述生态工程相比，另一种提高经济作物可攫取潜能的方法，或许更具争议，那就是基因改造（GM）。这一实践在20世纪晚期扎根，背景是DNA结构的发现，以及随后开展的基因切割与重组科学实验。在“绿色革命”之后，随着大豆、玉米、棉花、油菜及其他种植园商品作物的大规模农业在全球南方兴起，人们开发转基因作物，以获得更强的除草剂耐受性和抗虫性；后来，农学与政策话语广泛把它们推广为维系发展中国家粮食安全的关键（Conway 2012）。然而，它们的扩散一直在多个层面受到质疑，而且这种争议仍在继续。这些质疑包括：转基因作物可能危害消费者健康与环境健康；可能损害原住民的植物和农业知识产权及申请专利的机会；可能不利于小农增强经济自主能力和进入市场；以及它们对植物自身意味着什么——植物作为生命形式，正受到主要由企业主导、伦理上存在疑问的农业生物技术操控与同质化。

en: The complex entanglements of science and democracy at the heart of the GM tide come to light in India, where insect-resistant Bt cotton introduced in 2002 by the American agrochemical and agricultural biotechnology company Monsanto in partnership with the local firm Mahyco now occupies over 90 per cent of local farms, with negative effects not only on small and marginal farmers’ economic independence from global and national seed corporations companies but also on cotton’s own resilience resulting from the substitution of sturdier, older varieties with more fragile, longer-staple hybrids (Aga 2022). In Argentina, where genetically modified soybeans cover half of the country’s arable land and constitute a third of total exports, GM crops are celebrated in public discourse as heralds of modernization and economic growth within the so-called ‘soy boom’. This discourse, however, sits alongside stark realities of social and environmental injustice. Power, land, and profit are increasingly concentrated in the hands of a small agribusiness elite, and traditional crops are systematically replaced with plantation commodities, with dire consequences for local food security, forest ecosystems, rural livelihoods, and the health of communities exposed to the agrochemicals required to combat GM soy’s growing herbicide resistance (Leguizamón 2020).
zh: 转基因浪潮核心处科学与民主之间的复杂纠缠，在印度显露出来。2002年，美国农化与农业生物技术公司孟山都同印度本土公司Mahyco合作引入抗虫Bt棉花，如今它已占据当地90%以上的农场。这不仅损害了小农与边缘农户相对于全球及本国种子公司的经济独立性，也损害了棉花自身的韧性，因为更加健壮的旧品种被较脆弱、纤维较长的杂交品种取代（Aga 2022）。在阿根廷，转基因大豆覆盖了全国一半的可耕地，并占出口总额的三分之一。在所谓“大豆热潮”中，公共话语将转基因作物赞颂为现代化与经济增长的先驱。然而，与这种话语并存的，是社会与环境不正义的严酷现实。权力、土地和利润越来越集中于少数农业企业精英之手，传统作物被系统性地替换为种植园商品作物，给当地粮食安全、森林生态系统和乡村生计带来严重后果。为应对转基因大豆日益增强的除草剂抗性而使用的农化品，也危害了暴露于这些化学品的社群的健康（Leguizamón 2020）。
body.review: 底本确为“over90 per cent of local farms”，未在本句限定为棉田面积；另有“seed corporations companies”的重复表达，英文保留。句末“GM soy’s growing herbicide resistance”的主语亦依底本保留；它与对抗性杂草的通常表述不同，尚不能在未核对所引专著前直接把“大豆”改成“杂草”。

en: In other instances, the implications of GM crops for human health, together with their degree of cultivability in different ecological milieus, have long been under question. This is evidenced in the Philippines through the case of the much-promoted Golden Rice, a beta carotene-enhanced strain that promised to curb Vitamin A deficiency-related diseases and save millions of lives in the Third World but that remained at the trialling and pre-regulatory stage for almost a quarter of a century until 2022, when it first entered commercial production. Following this development, civil society organizations including Greenpeace and local farmer collectives, voiced concerns to the Supreme Court over the threat of biodiversity contamination and economic marginalization posed by the genetically engineered and patented crop to the estimated 7,000 unique traditional rice varieties grown, consumed, and sold by independent smallholders across the country’s biodiverse rice landscape. Given the existing and anticipated impacts of climate change, these actors also highlighted the serious risks posed by the reliance on a single-crop system for communities’ socio-economic resilience (Stone & Glover 2016; Fabro 2023). The appeal led to a court decision in May 2024 that halted the cultivation of Golden Rice in the Philippines. While celebrated by its proponents, the decision subsequently prompted widespread condemnation over the tens of thousands of children’s deaths that would potentially result from the blocking of what some segments of the scientific community hailed as the ‘lifesaver’ crop (McKie 2024) – even as on the long-term, monocrop plantations have proven a severe threat not only to local ecosystems, but also to the food security, dietary health, and nutritional wellbeing of local communities (Chao 2025).
zh: 在另一些情形中，转基因作物对人类健康的影响，以及它们在不同生态环境中的可栽培程度，长期受到质疑。菲律宾大力推广的黄金大米，就是一例。这种β-胡萝卜素含量得到提高的水稻品系，曾承诺遏制与维生素A缺乏有关的疾病，并拯救第三世界数百万人的生命，但在近四分之一个世纪里始终停留于试验和监管批准之前的阶段，直到2022年才首次进入商业生产。此后，包括绿色和平组织和当地农民团体在内的民间社会组织，向最高法院提出关切：全国生物多样性丰富的稻作景观中，独立小农种植、食用和出售着约七千种独特的传统水稻品种，而这种受到基因工程改造并被授予专利的作物，可能对它们造成生物多样性污染和经济边缘化的威胁。考虑到气候变化已经发生和预期将发生的影响，这些行动者还强调，依赖单一作物体系，会给社群的社会经济韧性带来严重风险（Stone & Glover 2016；Fabro 2023）。这一诉求促成了2024年5月的一项法院裁决，叫停了菲律宾的黄金大米种植。尽管支持这一裁决的人为之庆贺，裁决随后也引发广泛谴责：阻止种植这种被部分科学界人士誉为“救命者”的作物，可能导致数以万计的儿童死亡（McKie 2024）。而与此同时，从长远来看，单一作物种植园已经被证明，不仅严重威胁当地生态系统，也严重威胁当地社群的粮食安全、膳食健康与营养福祉（Chao 2025）。
body.review: 底本裁决月份为2024年5月。菲律宾水稻研究所的案件说明及2024年4月20日声明表明，上诉法院的相关判决日期为4月17日，该所于4月19日收到判决；本文保留底本月份并标明差异。关于作物效果、风险及可能死亡人数的论断，分别依作者与其所述争议各方的立场译出，不将预测写成已经发生的结果。

en: 2.4 Resistance and Failure
zh: 2.4　抵抗与失败

en: The Golden Rice controversy described above offers a segue into another important facet of plantation extractivism – namely, the ways in which extractivism is resisted at the grassroots and beyond, and the ways in which it can fail despite the seemingly relentless and ubiquitous force of technocapitalism and attendant state-corporate agendas. Indeed, the naturalization (in literal and figurative terms) of plantation logic, while indisputably pervasive and powerful in its reach and effects, has never gone entirely uncontested by those subject to its violence, nor have its extractive machinations always run as smoothly as might appear on the surface (Wolford 2021; Chao, Krupa & Li 2023). Human collectives have forged alliances in the face of plantation occupation, sometimes spanning countries and continents in terms of their membership, their activities encompassing concerted protest, multi-pronged advocacy, and strategic negotiation, as well as everyday, passive forms of resistance, including foot-dragging, theft, sabotage, non-compliance, and carefully cultivated inefficiency (Stoler 1985; Peluso 1992; Lewis 1996). Non-human entities, too, have in perhaps less intentional ways undermined the plantation project through their biotic affordances, including parasites that compromise the yields and productivity of monoculture cash crops rendered vulnerable to pathogenic attacks as a result of their genetic homogeneity. Perhaps most striking among these forms of resistance are those that involve the emergence of interspecies solidarities in the face of plantation extraction. In these emergences, the agendas of exploited humans and non-humans have aligned and become the unexpected grounds for new configurations of plantation subjecthood, victimhood, justice, and repair that are anchored not in rigid speciesist divides but rather in a counter-hegemonic blurring of animality, vegetality, and humanity.
zh: 上述黄金大米争议，把我们引向种植园攫取主义的另一个重要面向：草根层面及其他层面如何抵抗攫取主义，以及尽管技术资本主义及相伴而生的国家—企业议程似乎势不可挡、无处不在，攫取主义又如何可能失败。事实上，种植园逻辑的自然化——无论字面意义还是比喻意义——在其覆盖范围和影响力上无疑广泛而强大，但那些遭受其暴力的人从未完全放弃争辩与抵抗；它的攫取机制，也并非总像表面上看起来那样顺畅运行（Wolford 2021；Chao, Krupa & Li 2023）。面对种植园的占据，人类集体结成了联盟，有时其成员跨越国家乃至大陆。它们的行动包括协同抗议、多管齐下的倡议与策略性谈判，也包括日常的、消极形式的抵抗，如拖延、偷窃、破坏、不服从，以及刻意维持的低效率（Stoler 1985；Peluso 1992；Lewis 1996）。非人存在也通过其生物能力，以或许较少出于意图的方式，削弱种植园工程。例如，单一种植的经济作物由于遗传同质性而易受病原体侵袭，寄生生物就会损害其产量与生产率。这些抵抗形式中，或许最引人注目的，是面对种植园攫取而涌现的跨物种团结。在这些涌现中，受剥削的人类与非人的诉求相互契合，意外成为重新配置种植园主体地位、受害地位、正义与修复的基础。这种基础并不依靠僵硬的物种主义区隔，而在于以反霸权的方式，使动物性、植物性和人性之间的界线变得模糊。

en: In some instances, it was the ecologies within and upon which plantations were established that pushed against colonial visions of order, discipline, and homogeneity. In the American plantation zone, for instance, the prevalence of dense tropical vegetation and impenetrable swamplands, bayous, rivers, and wetlands often proved quasi-impossible for imperial powers to successfully map or control. Heat, diseases, vines, snakes, and insects joined forces with ancestors, spirits, and humans as a collective, animate force that repurposed the putative animality of exploited, racialized bodies into a source of resistance and revolution, and that became the birthing ground for enduring botanico-religious cosmologies including Obeah, Vodou, and Santería (Allewaert 2013). These unruly, more-than-human, and more-than-natural ecologies significantly impeded the productivity of imperial ventures at the same time as they became precious shelters for diasporic Africans fleeing capture and enslavement, generating a fleeting Black commons and precious multispecies refuge from the topographies of plantation violence (Hosbey & Roane 2021).
zh: 在一些情况下，种植园赖以建立并置身其中的生态，反过来抗拒了殖民者对秩序、纪律与同质性的想象。例如，在美洲种植园地带，茂密的热带植被，以及难以穿越的沼泽、河汊、河流和湿地广泛存在，帝国势力往往几乎不可能成功地测绘或控制它们。炎热、疾病、藤蔓、蛇和昆虫，同祖先、灵体及人类结合为一股具有生命活力的集体力量，把强加于受剥削、被种族化身体之上的所谓动物性，转用为抵抗与革命的源泉；这里也成为奥比亚、伏都和桑特里亚等绵延至今的植物—宗教宇宙观的诞生地（Allewaert 2013）。这些不受控制、超越人类、也超越自然的生态，显著妨碍了帝国事业的生产率；与此同时，它们又成为流散非洲人逃避捕捉和奴役的宝贵庇护所，在种植园暴力的地理空间中，生成短暂的黑人公地与珍贵的多物种避难之地（Hosbey & Roane 2021）。

en: Other interspecies solidarities arose within the confines of the plantation itself. In Jamaican sugarcane fields, for example, sorghum shoots were celebrated in the songs of enslaved Africans and became active, non-human participants in scenes of artistic and ecological commoning alongside tea, water, yams, and provision grounds (Dillon 2019). In the colonial indigo plantations of South Carolina and the Low Country, dark dyes seeped deep into the hands of enslaved women labourers, merging with fungible Black bodies in the making of porous part-human, part-vegetal flesh and generating new multispecies companionships, forged amidst and against the dehumanizing violence of the plantation system (King 2019: 111–140). On plantations across the Caribbean and the American South, food plots sown with root crops, plantains, bananas, and medicinal herbs, and cultivated by the enslaved, became unexpected biocultural havens that nurtured oppositional modes of Black life. The cultivation and celebration of these plots were anchored in understandings of the Earth and of the land as a goddess, bound in relations of reciprocal nourishment with humans and bringing humans and non-humans together in socio-ecological and cosmo-spiritual assemblages of kinship, repair, and care (Wynter 1971; Trouillot 2002; Davis et al. 2019). In other instances, non-humans became precious allies in processes of flight and fugitivity, or what has come to be known as marronage. These included rice seeds, black-eyed peas, cassava cuttings, and many other vegetal organisms that enslaved women in Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil, and the broader Caribbean carefully concealed in their braided hair before Trans-Atlantic crossing (Carney 2004; Keeve 2020; van Andel, Maat & Pinas 2023). Women then planted these seeds to feed themselves and their children during their escape from colonial plantations, their actions playing a vital role in supporting the food security and social continuity of newly formed escaped slave communities, or Maroons, and also transforming the broader ecological landscapes within which these communities gained ground and grew.
zh: 另一些跨物种团结，则在种植园自身的范围内兴起。例如，在牙买加甘蔗田里，高粱新芽受到被奴役非洲人歌谣的赞颂，并与茶、水、薯蓣和口粮地一起，成为艺术与生态共同化场景中积极参与的非人存在（Dillon 2019）。在南卡罗来纳及低地地区殖民时期的靛蓝种植园中，深色染料渗入受奴役女工的双手，与被当作可替换之物的黑人身体融合，形成一种边界可渗透、半人半植物的肉身，并生成新的多物种伙伴关系；这种关系诞生于种植园制度的非人化暴力之中，也与之对抗（King 2019: 111–140）。在加勒比地区与美国南部各处种植园里，受奴役者耕种着根茎作物、大蕉、香蕉及药草的食用作物小块田地，意外成为生物—文化的庇护所，滋养了具有对抗性的黑人生活方式。对这些田地的耕种与赞颂，植根于这样一种理解：把地球与土地视为女神，她与人类处于相互滋养的关系之中，并在人类与非人之间，建立起关乎亲缘、修复与照料的社会—生态及宇宙—精神组合体（Wynter 1971；Trouillot 2002；Davis et al. 2019）。在另一些情形中，非人成为逃离与逃亡过程——也就是后来所谓marronage——中珍贵的盟友。这些盟友包括稻种、黑眼豇豆、木薯插条及许多其他植物生物体。苏里南、法属圭亚那、巴西和更广泛加勒比地区的受奴役女性，在横渡大西洋之前，把它们小心藏在编起的头发中（Carney 2004；Keeve 2020；van Andel, Maat & Pinas 2023）。随后，这些女性在逃离殖民种植园的过程中，种下种子，以养活自己和孩子。她们的行动，对维系新形成的逃奴社群——即马龙社群——的粮食安全与社会延续起了至关重要的作用，也改变了这些社群立足并成长的更广阔生态景观。

en: More-than-human alliances continue to animate plantation landscapes of the present, including in ways that blur the line between the material and the metaphorical. In the Argentinian soy sector, for example, activists invoke resonances, similarities, and contiguities between the resistance of stubborn weeds like amaranth to the herbicide glyphosate and their own collective struggle to oppose the expansion of GM crops. Here, the resilience of amaranth lends momentum to human protests that come to mirror the plant’s own refusal to comply with the agendas of genetically engineered cash crop projects (Beilin & Suryanarayanan 2017). A similar plant-human indexicality is at play in the Papuan oil palm industry, where parasites, including rats, porcupines, coconut caterpillars, the Ganoderma fungus, and the Rhinoceros beetle, are often celebrated by Indigenous anti-plantation activists as more-than-human arbiters or agents of retributive justice for the damages inflicted by the relentlessly expanding agribusiness sector, their slow, often invisible, yet highly effective actions in turn inspiring human resistance to oil palm monocrops and their colonial-capitalist undergirdings (Chao 2021b). In the Indian tea sector, meanwhile, workers’ resistance to the surplus and unrecognized labour and time required of them to achieve the demands of organic cultivation both affects and is affected by non-human agency. Intentionally inconsistent tea-plucking on the part of workers, for example, results in an overgrowth of stubborn yet edible fiddlehead ferns. This generates unruly ecosystems that defy the control and discipline of the plantation regime, at the same time as it creates precious foraging grounds that support the food security and nutritional diversity of plantation labourers (Kumpf 2021).
zh: 超越人类的联盟，继续赋予当今种植园景观以活力，其中一些方式使物质与隐喻之间的界线变得模糊。例如，在阿根廷的大豆产业中，行动者把苋属等顽强杂草对除草剂草甘膦的抗性，同自身反对转基因作物扩张的集体斗争联系起来，强调二者之间的共鸣、相似与邻接关系。在这里，苋属植物的韧性为人类抗议增添了动力，抗议仿佛映照着植物自身对基因工程经济作物项目议程的不服从（Beilin & Suryanarayanan 2017）。在巴布亚油棕产业中，一种相似的植物—人类指示性关系也在发挥作用。老鼠、豪猪、椰树毛虫、灵芝属真菌和犀金龟等寄生生物，常被反种植园的原住民行动者赞颂为超越人类的仲裁者或报应正义的执行者，对不断扩张的农业企业部门造成的损害施以惩罚。它们缓慢、往往不可见却高度有效的行动，反过来激励人类抵抗油棕单一种植及其殖民—资本主义基础（Chao 2021b）。与此同时，在印度茶业中，为满足有机栽培要求，工人被迫付出额外且不获承认的劳动与时间；他们对此的抵抗，既影响非人能动性，也受到后者影响。例如，工人故意不规律地采茶，导致顽强却可食用的卷芽蕨类大量滋长。这既生成了违抗种植园体制控制与纪律的不驯生态系统，又创造了宝贵的采集场所，支持种植园劳动者的粮食安全与营养多样性（Kumpf 2021）。

en: In other cases, non-human partners involved or invoked by people affected by monocultural extractivism transcend the realm of the biotic and material, pointing to the more-than-secular dimensions of plantation lifeworlds. In Eastern Borneo, for example, spirit communication and customary healing rituals have played a major role in sustaining a sense of self and sociality among Indigenous Luangan communities, whose environments have been radically transformed by oil palm but who find, in encounters with spirits, a powerful means to alleviate everyday experiences of unpredictability and alienation (Hermanns 2020). In a comparable vein, alliances forged with outsiders by Indigenous Makushi communities in Guyana to oppose rubber expansion operate in conjunction to long-standing relationships with shamans, whose ability to communicate with and harness the powers of spirits lends a powerful, cosmological dimension to Makushi struggles for justice in the face of ongoing land dispossession and occupation (Whitaker 2020).
zh: 在另一些情况下，受到单一种植攫取主义影响的人们所结交或召唤的非人伙伴，超出了生物与物质的领域，指向种植园生活世界超越世俗的维度。例如，在婆罗洲东部，同灵体交流以及遵循习惯的治疗仪式，对于卢安甘原住民社群维系自我感和社会关系，发挥了重要作用。油棕已彻底改变他们的环境，但他们在与灵体相遇时，找到了一种有力途径，缓解日常生活中不可预测与疏离的体验（Hermanns 2020）。类似地，在圭亚那，马库希原住民社群为了反对橡胶扩张而与外来者结成的联盟，同他们长期以来与萨满的关系共同发挥作用。萨满能够同灵体交流并调动其力量，为马库希人在持续的土地剥夺和占据中争取正义的斗争，赋予了强有力的宇宙观维度（Whitaker 2020）。

en: The potency of more-than-human resistance to, or non-compliance with, the extractive visions of plantation logic manifests perhaps most strikingly in instances where monocrop projects have collapsed entirely or been abandoned due to unsurmountable environmental and ecosystemic factors. In Brazil, for instance, efforts to defeat the South American Leaf Blight – a type of fungus that has proved remarkably resistant to chemical treatment, grafting, and plant breeding – have been consistently ineffective, in turn shattering the country’s visions of establishing itself as a leading industrial rubber producer (Dean 1987). Relentless attacks by mites, lace bugs, caterpillars, and various other endemic tropical critters were also partly responsible for the dramatic collapse of ‘Fordlandia’, a grandiose, if entirely unrealistic, project initiated by American business magnate Henry Ford in the early twentieth century and aiming to bring plantation-scale rubber production to the Amazon jungle, alongside the construction of midwestern-style towns, hospitals, railroads, power plants, golf courses, and tennis courts. After almost twenty years of thwarted efforts to control an environment completely unfit for monocrop rubber cultivation, the entire operation was sold by Ford to Brazilian buyers for a tenth of what it had cost to establish (Grandin 2010).
zh: 超越人类的抵抗，或对种植园逻辑之攫取愿景的不服从，其力量或许在这样一些情形中表现得最为鲜明：由于无法克服的环境与生态系统因素，单一作物项目彻底崩溃，或遭到放弃。例如，在巴西，对付南美叶疫病的努力始终收效甚微。这种真菌对化学处理、嫁接及植物育种显示出极强的抵抗力，从而粉碎了巴西成为主要工业化橡胶生产国的愿景（Dean 1987）。螨虫、网蝽、毛虫及其他各种当地热带小生物的持续袭击，也是“福特兰迪亚”惨败的部分原因。这个宏大却完全不切实际的项目，由美国商业巨头亨利·福特在20世纪初发起，旨在把种植园规模的橡胶生产带进亚马孙丛林，并配套建设美国中西部风格的城镇、医院、铁路、发电厂、高尔夫球场与网球场。在近二十年里，人们试图控制一个完全不适合橡胶单一种植的环境，却一再受挫；最终，福特以相当于创建成本十分之一的价格，把整个项目卖给了巴西买家（Grandin 2010）。
body.review: 底本把South American Leaf Blight直接说成“一种真菌”；译文保留其行文关系，但病名与致病真菌并非同一概念，所指是由真菌导致的橡胶树南美叶疫病。

en: The dramatic consequences of neglecting ecological factors have more recently been exemplified by the 1997–1998 Indonesian Mega Rice Project in Central Borneo. Initiated by the government and aimed at transforming one million hectares of peat swamp forest into rice paddy fields, the project was, from the outset, marred by the nutrient-poor nature of local peat soils, the unsuitability of Borneo’s ecosystems for wet rice cultivation, and the struggles experienced by the imported labour force to manage an unfamiliar environment. The disturbance and drainage of tropical peat soils, compounded by a year of extreme drought during the El Niño event, resulted in peat fires spreading uncontrollably under and overground and generating in the space of a few months the same amount of carbon dioxide as an estimated 13–40 per cent of global annual carbon emissions from fossil fuels (Goldstein 2016). Abandoned within two years, the Mega Rice Project has been recognized as one of the most devastating environmental disasters in Indonesia’s history, at the same time as it produced almost no rice.
zh: 较近时期，1997—1998年印度尼西亚在婆罗洲中部推行的“百万公顷稻田计划”，则展示了忽视生态因素会带来何等严重的后果。这个由政府发起的项目，旨在把一百万公顷泥炭沼泽林改造成稻田，但从一开始便困难重重：当地泥炭土缺乏养分，婆罗洲的生态系统不适宜水稻栽培，外来劳动力也难以应付陌生环境。热带泥炭土遭到扰动和排水，再叠加厄尔尼诺现象期间一整年的极端干旱，导致泥炭火灾在地上地下失控蔓延；仅仅数月之内，排放的二氧化碳量，据估计相当于全球化石燃料年碳排放的13%—40%（Goldstein 2016）。这一“百万公顷稻田计划”在两年内就被放弃，被视为印度尼西亚历史上最具破坏性的环境灾难之一，而它几乎没有产出任何稻米。
body.review: 13%—40%的数字须注意统计范围。Page等2002年《Nature》原始研究，是把中加里曼丹研究区的估算外推到1997年印度尼西亚全国泥炭和植被火灾后，得到相对于全球化石燃料年均碳排放的这一比例，不能直接理解为仅该稻田项目自身的排放量。底本的项目年代与归因表述保留。

en: 2.5 Conclusions
zh: 2.5　结论

en: The framing of the ‘Plantationocene’ outlined in the Introduction to this Element offers a useful analytic for thinking about extraction in multispecies terms. Rather than centring (and singularizing) the ‘human’ as the driver of ecological transformation (as in the ‘Anthropocene’) or relying on an abstracted notion of ‘capital’ as the root cause of environmental decline (as in the ‘Capitalocene’), the Plantationocene invites us to take seriously the complex entanglements of particular plants, particular plantations, and particular people within extractive landscapes, together with the congeries of species, symbiotes, and spirits that also partake in the making and unmaking of monocrop systems and societies. As I have demonstrated in this section, multispecies extraction has long been a defining feature in the rise (and, at times, fall) of plantation lifeworlds – from the forced removal and displacement of Indigenous Peoples and local communities from their ancestral and more-than-human territories, to the systematic extraction of labour from racialized bodies, themselves often uprooted from native soils, to the increasingly technologically mediated and engineered extraction of cash crops’ own biotic vitality as seeds of life and sources of profit. This multi-faceted, extractivist logic is premised on colonial-capitalist ideologies that assume the malleability of environments and the compliance of plantation subjects, as well as a rigid division of nature from culture.
zh: 本书导论提出的“种植园世”框架，为从多物种角度思考攫取提供了有用的分析工具。它并不像“人类世”那样，将“人类”置于生态转变的驱动中心，并把人类处理为单一主体；也不像“资本世”那样，依赖抽象化的“资本”概念，把它看成环境衰败的根本原因。种植园世邀请我们认真对待攫取性景观中具体植物、具体种植园与具体人群之间的复杂纠缠，以及同样参与建构和拆解单一种植体系与社会的种种物种、共生者和灵体。如本部分所示，多物种攫取长期以来就是种植园生活世界兴起——有时也衰落——的决定性特征：从强迫原住民族与当地社群离开其祖居且超越人类的领地，到系统性地从种族化身体中攫取劳动——这些身体本身也往往被迫离开故土——再到越来越多地借助技术中介和工程手段，攫取经济作物自身作为生命种子和利润来源的生物活力。这种多面的攫取主义逻辑，以殖民—资本主义意识形态为前提；后者既假定环境可以任意塑造、种植园主体必将服从，也假定自然与文化之间存在僵硬的分界。

en: And yet, as the final section of this section has shown, these dangerous fictions are belied by realities of resistance to plantation violence, many of which are grounded in interspecies indexicalities that muddy the boundaries between the human and the non-human as subjects of harm and agents of defiance. Attempts to simplify, control, and conjure plantations as capitalist natures have often failed due to ecological factors and biotic actors whose disruptive affordances are all too often underestimated in the design and implementation of anthropogenic landscape transformations (Scott 1998; Tsing 2015; Tsing, Mathews & Bubandt 2019). These factors and actors may not be considered intentional – and yet, they have often been harnessed and signified as such by human collectives within counter-plantation imaginaries, struggles, and solidarities. Retrieving sovereignty in the plantation, as such, has often entailed for communities the world over, a form of rallying-with the non-human in its myriad forms, anchored in a recognition of shared vulnerabilities and threatened futures across – and sometimes beyond – species lines.
zh: 然而，正如本部分最后一节所展示的，对种植园暴力的实际抵抗，戳破了这些危险的虚构。许多抵抗立足于跨物种的指示性关系，使人类与非人作为受害主体和反抗行动者之间的边界变得模糊。把种植园简化、控制并构想为资本主义自然的尝试，常常由于生态因素与生物行动者而失败。在设计和实施人为景观改造时，人们往往严重低估了这些因素与行动者扰乱既定安排的能力（Scott 1998；Tsing 2015；Tsing, Mathews & Bubandt 2019）。这些因素与行动者或许不被视为具有意图，然而，在反种植园的想象、斗争与团结中，人类集体却常常把它们当作具有意图者来动员，并赋予它们这种意义。因此，对世界各地的社群而言，在种植园中夺回主权，常常意味着一种同千姿百态的非人存在共同集结的行动。这种行动植根于对共同脆弱性和受威胁未来的认识，跨越物种界线，有时甚至超出以物种划界的方式。
